title: Coherence Lengths of Laser Pointers
abstract: We report on the coherence lengths of low-cost green laser pointers in the midst of multimodal behavior using an optical interferometer based on noncollinear beam geometries and a CMOS detector array. Examined devices include three diode lasers and a frequency-doubled neodymium-emission diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) laser. Coherence length measurements are variable among devices, but values can nevertheless regularly exceed 10 cm. The work serves as a template for an advanced undergraduate physics laboratory experiment and may inspire new kinds of laser pointer devices utilizing interference effects as operative principles.

title: Lecture Board Readability as an AI-Measurable Predictor of Perceived Teaching Clarity
abstract: Lecture boards remain central to university teaching in physics and mathematics, yet the visual quality of what instructors write has rarely been measured systematically. We examined whether a vision-language model can score board writing in a way that relates to how students perceive instruction. We analysed 2,645 board images from 56 university physics and applied mathematics courses taught by 18 lecturers, scoring each image 50 times with Claude 3.5 Sonnet on readability, organization and visual elements. Course-level readability was associated with student-rated clarity ($r$ = .43) and organization ($r$ = .46), and remained the only significant predictor of the overall survey score after controlling for class size, mean course grade and study year. These associations were robust to clustering by lecturer and remained stable when only one or two images per lecture were used. In a subsample of 100 images rated by four human raters, agreement between AI and human scores was comparable to agreement among the raters themselves for visual elements, lower for readability and weakest for organization. Student evaluations served as a benchmark of perceived clarity rather than of teaching quality as a whole. Automated analysis of board images may offer a low-cost, scalable source of formative feedback in STEM teaching.

title: Navigating Quantum Education at the University level: Pedagogical Pathways and a Roadmap for Textbook Selection
abstract: Instruction in quantum mechanics (QM) is often categorized by its entry point as 'wave-first' or 'spin-first', yet these labels lack consistent definitions and overlook other established or emerging approaches. Moreover, while capturing broad differences in topic selection and sequencing, this binary framing obscures critical differences in contextualization--how three dimensions (mathematical tools, phenomena and experiments, and theoretical concepts) are framed and connected to support student sensemaking. Research also rarely examines how such pedagogical choices unfold across the undergraduate-to-graduate trajectory. Using textbooks as an analytical lens to map these choices and characterize overarching pathways, encompassing entry points and overall orientations, we comparatively analyze the selection, sequencing, and contextualization of core topics across these 3 dimensions, alongside prefaces and introductions, in 36 university QM textbooks spanning countries and eras. At the topic level, we show that identical topics occupy widely different curricular roles depending on their contextualization. Synthesizing these findings into pathways, we identify three additional entry-point archetypes (labeled path-, qubit-, and axiom-first) and characterize all 5 approaches, showing that most textbooks combine multiple archetypes in their opening chapters. Extending this synthesis beyond entry points, we map textbooks' overall orientations relative to mathematics, experiment and application, and theoretical physics. Interpreting these profiles alongside authors' rationales reveals how educators navigate competing trade-offs among mathematical accessibility, theoretical generality, physical motivation, and modern developments. This study provides a multidimensional framework, substantive examples, and a practical roadmap for textbook selection and curriculum design in QM education.
